title: Checklist 3

lessons.title: Course Material: Checklist (3).pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Maximize Your Productivity – Checklist  Introduction ü Most people’s biggest problem is getting everything done on their list ü You get more done by making the best of the time you have ü Learn tools and techniques for maximizing productivity in your business and personal lives  The Basics of Productivity ü Identify obstacles that slow you down and remove them ü Things we face every day and may not be aware of ü Manage your time and identify ‘drains’ ü Self-awareness is key ü Monitor your schedule ü Use data to make changes  Learning Objectives:  ü Set your goals and plan in advance, so you can reduce distractions and improve your focus  ü Identify your natural rhythms and energy cycles so that you can work with them rather than against them. ü Identify and manage the biggest drains on your time so that you know where you need to improve scheduling, delegation and automation.

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  ü Implement tips on tidying up and organizing so that you have a clean and efficient workspace. ü Implement tactics to be more selective, so you spend your time on the most important tasks. ü Apply best practices to stay in optimal health with minimal effort so that you're in the best physical and mental shape possible. ü Test specific tools to find the best ones for you so that you can enhance and optimize your productivity. ü Consolidate and implement your learning and plan future action steps so you can achieve the goals you set for this course  ü This course is a productivity toolbox ü You can put a lot to use immediately ü Some techniques will work well, others may not be for you   Action Steps: 1. We'll get into it all in much more detail later, but for now, take a few minutes to think about your current way of working. Ask yourself: a. How do you spend the bulk of your time each day? b. Where do you feel that you're not being productive? c. How would you rather be spending your time each day? d. What are some things you already feel are time wasters?      You don't need perfect answers… just some ideas to get the ball rolling

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  Module 1 – Improve Your Focus  Learning Objective: ü Set your goals and plan in advance, so you can reduce distractions and improve your focus   ü Gaining and maintaining focus is a major part of productivity ü If you have too much going on at once, you will lose focus ü Without focus, things don’t get done well or quickly  Focus on Goals ü Start with establishing clear goals ü The task in hand needs to be at the forefront of your mind ü Stay focused to ignore distractions  Create a Prioritized To-Do List ü Extrapolate smaller goals and specific tasks from your goals ü Focus on one task at a time ü Take a large goal and make a list of everything that needs to be done in order to achieve it ü Isolate the most important item ü Put that, and then the items following in importance, at the top ü Assign a deadline to each list item to prioritize

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  One To-Do List ü Only have one to-do list to maintain simplicity ü Put everything together ü Prioritize different item categories  Eliminate Non-Essentials ü Many people add too much clutter ü You can put non-essentials in a second list ü Set a limit on list items  Schedule Time for Focus ü Time has an important relationship with focus ü Set aside time to accomplish a task ü Take long-term tasks and break them into bite-sized chunks  Stop Multi-Tasking ü Multi-tasking helps get things done is a myth ü It ruins your focus ü Only work on one task at a time  Know the Warning Signs ü Learn to recognize the signs of when you’ve lost focus ü If you feel it coming on, set your work aside ü Get up and relax to give your brain a break

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  Identify Other Focus Killers ü Try to identify and develop strategies for other focus killers ü Turn off distracting electronics notifications ü Arrange your schedule around unavoidable distractions  Develop a Pre-Work Ritual ü The best way to harness focus is to create a pre-work ritual ü Get yourself into the right state of mind ü Yoga, meditation, listening to music, or reading a book   Action Steps: 1. Identify which things make you lose your focus during the day. For each of these ‘focus killers’, note which tips from the chapter you’re going to implement to improve your focus, and how you’ll use them.

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6   Module 2 – Discover Your Rhythms  Learning Objective: ü Identify your natural rhythms and energy cycles so that you can work with them rather than against them.  ü You have times of the day that are more or less productive ü It’s important to discover these natural energy rhythms ü You may be working against them so identify the right times of day for the right tasks  How to Discover Your Rhythms ü You may already have some idea ü Monitor your feelings and energy level throughout the day ü Decide on a regular time throughout the day to ‘check in’ ü Jot down a quick note about how you’re feeling ü Create a numbered indication system ü After a week or two you’ll see patterns emerge   Rearrange Your Schedule ü Arrange your schedule differently each week ü Switch up times that you dedicate to certain tasks

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  ü Experience different work patterns first-hand to see what works best  Establish Routines ü Take data and create a schedule from it ü Your mind and body get used to doing the same thing in a routine ü Expected behaviours make focusing easier ü Plug tasks into categories ü Create your schedule around these categories to help with focus ü Identify level of focus required for each category    Action Steps: 1. Identify your energy levels at different times of day. Note what work you prefer to do at those times of day.  2. Based on your high-energy and low energy times, outline a morning, mid-day, and evening routine to follow.

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Module 3 – Manage Time Drains  Learning Objective: ü Identify and manage the biggest drains on your time so that you know where you need to improve scheduling, delegation and automation.  ü Another way to improve productivity is to remove blocks ü Time drains aren’t necessarily time wasters ü They’re things you need to control and keep in check  Email ü Email is important, but can also be a time drain ü Establish a time during the day for handling emails ü Create a schedule for reading and responding ü For longer responses, let the person know that you’ll send a detailed reply later on ü Add urgent emails to your to-do list ü Decide on its priority level ü Set a time limit for looking at emails ü Organize your inbox with folders by priority ü Create an ‘away’ message and email templates  The Internet ü The internet offers a wealth of distractions ü Keep one goal in mind when you’re online

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  ü Bookmark distractions to go back to later ü Social media is a dangerous time drain ü Log in only when you’re able to focus for a certain amount of time ü Turn off notifications  Phone Calls ü You may have no choice but to answer the phone ü Minimize negative effects by keeping calls focused on business ü Schedule a time to phone back calls that aren’t urgent  Meetings ü Keep meetings to a minimum and only discuss issues that can’t be easily discussed via email ü Organize short meetings with a clear start and end time ü Create a detailed agenda to stay focused on important business ü You can hold virtual meetings so that everyone doesn’t have to be present ü Agree on a regular meeting time each week or month ü Save things that need to be discussed for these meetings  Coworkers ü Create an environment where you’re physically isolated to cut down on distractions from coworkers ü Don’t be afraid to say No ü Schedule times to chat as a break from work focus

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  Mundane Tasks ü Mundane, yet essential, tasks take away from more important tasks ü To get rid of these tasks: o Eliminate o Delegate o Outsource o Automate  Mindless Entertainment ü A great number of drains are mindless entertainment ü We need these distractions to give us pleasure and take our minds off things ü It’s ok to spend some time with these activities if you’re in control ü Indulge in fun activities during breaks ü Make sure you can easily pull yourself away and get back to work ü Set aside a certain time of day to indulge

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11  Action Steps: 1. Review your answers to all the activities you’ve completed so far. Can you identify any patterns that show where your biggest time drains are?  2. If not, try tracking exactly what you spend your time on each day for a week and add up the time for each task. You can use a simple notepad, or a tool like Evernote. 3. Then, make a list of which items are taking up too much of your time relative to their importance for achieving your goals. 4. Note which tips from this chapter you’re going to implement to eliminate or reduce these time drains.

PAGE_12:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 12  Module 4 – Get Organized  Learning Objective: ü Apply tips on tidying up and organizing so that you have a clean and efficient workspace  ü A clean and tidy workspace leads to better productivity ü Most people find it easier to focus when things are tidy ü Reduce clutter  Keep Surfaces Clean ü Surfaces are where clutter is most likely to accumulate ü Create whatever filing system you want ü Make sure surfaces stay clean  Put it Away ü Put things away as soon as you’re done using them ü Put them in the right place ü Get into a habit of doing this  Go Paperless ü There’s little need for paper in today’s digital office ü Scan files and store them digitally ü This is also good for the environment

PAGE_13:
IAPWE Professional
